newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IBM SAYS NEEDS HUNGARY/WTO AGREEMENTS.
newsitem.headline: IBM SAYS NEEDS HUNGARY/WTO AGREEMENTS.

text.p: Visiting IBM officials told Hungarian Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy the fact that Hungary is yet to sign two World Trade Organisation (WTO) agreements hinders IBM Hungary's exports to the U.S.

"We informed Mr. Medgyessy that this becomes important as...for contracts with the U.S. government, those treaties are required," Walter Meizer, General Manager of Germany's IBM Speichersysteme GmbH, a unit of IBM Storage Systems Division, told a news conference.

Dieter Munk, General Manager of IBM's Hungarian hard drive plant in Szekesfehervar, in western Hungary, said the U.S. gives preferential treatment to those importers who have signed the WTO agreements on general purchases and information technology.
Munk said IBM had invested some $100 million in Hungary since early 1995 and by the end of 1997 will have created over 3,500 jobs directly or through IBM projects.
The Hungarian plant assembles and tests 3.5-inch disk drives for desktop computers and 2.5-inch drives for mobile appliances.

The parts come from southeast Asia, Germany and Italy and the final product is exported, 40 percent of it to IBM's own PC companies and 60 percent to other manufacturers. Munk said that in 1996 some 60 percent of the plant's exports went to the U.S.
Last year the plant produced one million disk drives and IBM plans to triple output this year.
